events.title: The nine hearths raise Seonaid Chiar to the flame
events.body: The nine hearths of Dùn ìseal raise Seonaid Chiar of the house of Muireach to the flame at six-and-twenty years old, the youngest Keeper chosen since Muireach Liath's own day. Her grandmother, a cutter of the galleries all her working life, warns her that a young Keeper who bends once in her first year is asked to bend again for the rest of her keeping.

events.title: Three teachers of Cnoc bhàn set an unlit lamp before the Hall's door
events.body: Three old teachers of the stag's school at Cnoc bhàn climb the mountain road on foot and set an unlit lamp on the stones before Talla na Lasrach, asking only to be let back among the cutters already working the galleries, and swearing to ask nothing of the vein aloud if the Hall will stop asking whether they have any right to stand near it.

events.title: Seonaid Chiar's guild judgment at Cnoc leathan
events.body: Hearing two carriers of Cnoc leathan's guild each accuse the other of taking a fee out of turn, Seonaid Chiar asks only which of them had first offered to give the disputed load back, and, hearing neither had, tells them the Hall's grant is a right to carry and not a right to quarrel. The two settle the matter themselves before they have gone a mile down the mountain road.

events.title: Ruairidh Glas stands once more before the stone cup
events.body: In his nine hundred and ninth year, Ruairidh Glas, holder of the Red Share, asks unasked leave to climb Dùn ìseal on foot and stand again before the stone cup, though no lord of a share is required to outside the quarter days. He says nothing aloud that any living ear catches, and goes back down the same evening to Dùn dhearg.

events.title: Ruairidh Glas dies at Dùn dhearg
events.body: Ruairidh Glas dies in his own bed at Dùn dhearg, having lived nine hundred and ten years and never once returned to Dùn thais since the morning he shed the first blood of the strife of the heirs there. He outlives every soul who stood beside him at the ford where his grandfather's line first took the Red Hill.

events.title: The Red Share passes without a summons to the Hall
events.body: Ruairidh Glas's son takes up the Red Share at Dùn dhearg without any summons to the Hall, as the Peace of the Threshold requires none where an heir is named and undisputed. The season's rolls, careful to name every lesser lord, stay strangely thin about naming this one, a silence the Hall's clerk lays to the household's own quiet rather than to any failure of the pen.

events.title: The four dead of the high gallery are buried on the Hall's own ground
events.body: The four cutters killed when the roof of the highest gallery falls at Dùn ìseal are carried up and buried on the Hall's own ground, the one ground on the island no feud has ever been let to follow a man. Seonaid Chiar sets the last stone over the last of them with her own hands, which no Keeper before her is remembered to have done.

events.title: The first oak props are cut for the galleries
events.body: After a season's argument over how a gallery roof should ever be held against another such fall, Seonaid Chiar orders timber props of oak set in every gallery the Hall works, the first timber the Hall has ever spent on the mountain itself. The first oak is felled and cut within the season, so that no gallery stands unpropped by the following year's cutting.

events.title: Seonaid Chiar dies above the galleries she kept
events.body: Seonaid Chiar dies in her own quarters above the galleries at Dùn ìseal, eighty-five years old, having held the flame the better part of six decades. The nine hearths that raised her young choose another after her without any dispute the rolls think worth setting down.

events.title: The school at Cnoc bhàn returns its unlit lamp
events.body: On word of Seonaid Chiar's death, the school at Cnoc bhàn sends no delegation and no message of grief, only the same unlit lamp its three old teachers once set before her door, carried back up by cutters young enough to have known no other Keeper, and left again on the same stones, still unlit.

events.title: Cathair dhomhain's shrine holds the Law to the grain
events.body: The new shrine at Cathair dhomhain keeps the Small-Burning Law to the very grain from its founding day, a strictness the town becomes known for beyond any other pride it holds. Lowland households speak of it for a lifetime, though the town itself remains a place carriers pass through on the way to somewhere else.

events.title: The death of Cailean
events.body: Cailean, a cousin of Goraidh mac Ìomhair through their grandmothers, dies under a wall he is mending at his own hall in a night of high wind. He leaves no child of his body, and his county of the east goes unclaimed.

events.title: The death of Donnchadh
events.body: Donnchadh, Cailean's younger brother, dies of a cough the hearth-women cannot cut, with his sister's hand in his. He too leaves no child, and the second of the three old counties east of Dùn dhearg is left without an heir named.

events.title: Goraidh's marriage to Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh
events.body: Goraidh mac Ìomhair rides to Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh, a widowed kinswoman of four hundred years who holds the third of the old eastern counties alone, and marries her in the spring. Her county comes whole into the marriage, as the Peace of the Threshold allows, and Goraidh takes on her dead husbands' debts to the county's smiths.

events.title: Goraidh rides the three counties
events.body: Through the first year of the marriage Goraidh mac Ìomhair walks the boundaries of all three gathered counties with Muirne beside him, eating at the hearths and not the halls, learning which streams have moved and which grazings are old enough to fight over.

events.title: The hungry harvests
events.body: Two summers running the rains come at the wrong end of the season and the barley rots standing in the low ground east of Dùn dhearg. Goraidh mac Ìomhair opens all four of his granaries and gives grain outright to nine households that cannot pay even the lowered price.

events.title: Death of Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh
events.body: Muirne nic Dhonnchaidh dies in her sleep in the ninth year of her marriage to Goraidh mac Ìomhair, with her own county's reciter in the room. He buries her among her own dead, as she asked him.

events.title: The timber hall of Dùn dhearg raised with a granary at each corner
events.body: Goraidh mac Ìomhair raises a long hall of squared oak on his father's rise at Dùn dhearg, with a granary at each of its four corners. The carpenters of the Red Share and of the three gathered counties raise it side by side, and the granaries are filled from all four counties in one season.

events.title: Goraidh leaves his spear at the last house
events.body: Come to answer the council's word, Goraidh mac Ìomhair leaves his spear with his men at the last waypoint house on the mountain road and climbs to Dùn ìseal on foot and unarmed.

events.title: The waypoint-keepers gather the road toll for a share
events.body: Goraidh does not gather the toll of one fish in twenty himself. He gives it to the keepers of the waypoint houses along each road, who have kept a bed and a fire for carriers since before his grandfather's day, and lets each keep a share of what they take.

events.title: A waypoint-keeper's short tally forgiven
events.body: At a waypoint house on the northern road a keeper's first season's toll comes in a tenth short, for want of anyone at the door by night. Goraidh mac Ìomhair laughs at the reckoning and lets the shortfall stand.

events.title: Mòrag takes up the walking of the roads
events.body: Goraidh's daughter Mòrag, who could never sit still in a hall, takes over the walking of the island's roads from her ageing father long before he will call it a handing-over. He lets her.

events.title: Dòmhnall's fall from the cart
events.body: Dòmhnall, riding the back board of a laden cart above the ford, is thrown under its wheel where it strikes a stone left standing proud of the road-bed. His leg is set and set again and never knits true; he walks with a stick the rest of his life.

events.title: Death of Goraidh Mòr
events.body: Goraidh mac Ìomhair dies in his own hall at Dùn dhearg in his two hundred and thirteenth year, in the granary month, asking after the notching of the western road's toll-sticks. His daughter Mòrag and two waypoint-keepers rendering their tallies are with him.

events.title: The toll-stick notched at Mòr nic Dhùghaill's old house
events.body: Days after Goraidh Mòr's death, the keeper of the old waypoint house that was Mòr nic Dhùghaill's notches a fresh toll-stick for a carrier's fish and a carrier's wool, as she has every week before and will every week after, whoever holds the hall at Dùn dhearg.

events.title: The toll-chest counted at a keeper's own door
events.body: Mòrag nan Rathad finds the toll-house two days east of the ford unanswered longest of all its keepers' letters. She has her road-guards open the keeper's own chest and counts the silver on a cloth before him, takes half for the mending, and leaves half for his household.

events.title: Mòrag meets Niall Òg on the northern road
events.body: On a wet stretch of the northern road, Mòrag nan Rathad shelters from rain beside an old man on a milestone: Niall Òg, grandson of Ailean Mòr, now past his sixteen hundredth year. He tells her his name and sits with her a while before going on afoot.

events.title: Niall Òg tells Mòrag of the cord
events.body: Niall Òg tells Mòrag nan Rathad of the cord of seven hundred and twelve knots laid on the floor at Dùn ìseal, and says she is the first of the line he has met who looks at the cord itself and not at her own knot in it.

events.title: The golden house opened free of toll
events.body: Mòrag nan Rathad opens the new waypoint house on the eastern road north of Seann Dunn with a night's feast for every carrier who can be reached in time, none of them charged the toll. Carriers call the new timber the golden house before it has weathered, and the name holds.

events.title: The bridge-foot town begins to grow
events.body: After the western crossing of the Abhainn dhomhain is widened for two laden carts abreast, the small fishing town at the bridge-foot below Dùn ìseal begins to grow in earnest, outgrowing three neighbouring towns within Mòrag nan Rathad's own lifetime.

events.title: Mòrag names Dòmhnall her heir
events.body: Mòrag nan Rathad has her lame son Dòmhnall carried the length of three road-stretches in a covered chair, then names him before the household at Dùn dhearg as her heir, past her hundred and sixtieth year herself.

events.title: Mòrag's last circuit of the roads
events.body: Against the advice of her household, Mòrag nan Rathad rides the whole western circuit in her hundred and eighty-ninth year, finding less to mend than in any year of her reign, and tells the waypoint-keepers so at every house she stops in.

events.title: Mòrag nan Rathad dies at Dùn dhearg
events.body: Mòrag nan Rathad dies at Dùn dhearg in the winter, a hundred and ninety-four years old, with her son beside her. Carriers from three days' distance come to stand outside the hall, and Dòmhnall feeds them from the golden house's own stores.

events.title: Niall Òg speaks over Mòrag's grave
events.body: At Mòrag nan Rathad's grave, Niall Òg says that of the seven hundred and twelve heirs he once watched knotted on the cord, she alone spent her life looking at the cord itself, and that her roads are the nearest thing since to that cord laid honestly on the ground.

events.title: Sìleas Dhonn finds the Ceann mhin rolls do not add
events.body: Dòmhnall Crùbach's young niece Sìleas Dhonn, asked to check the waypoint-keepers' tallies, finds three years in which the Ceann mhin keepers' own count does not match what passed through their gates, though never provably by theft. She keeps her own copy of the figures and says nothing of it while her uncle lives.

events.title: The scorpion's sting sworn on at a trade
events.body: At Baile àrsaidh a woman stung on the hand during a trade of cattle for salt fish finishes the bargain with her fingers still swelling, saying a hurt taken in the open is worth more than a promise given behind a closed door. Others take up her way of it, keeping a dried sting in a box to swear by.

events.title: The Hall's grain-carts reach Seann Chwen first
events.body: After the storm at Seann Chwen, the Keeper's grain-carts reach the ruined harbour a full day ahead of Dòmhnall Crùbach's, running the whole way on the road above the ford that Mòrag nan Rathad raised out of the mud in the first summer of her reign.

events.title: The sting first sworn on at a wider trade
events.body: The scorpion's-sting oath of Baile àrsaidh is sworn for the first time at a trade with an outside harbour town, at Ros bheag, carrying the custom beyond the settlement that began it.

events.title: Rònat sent to the stag's school
events.body: A boy of ten with a talent for losing count past thirty is sent from his father's holding to the stag's school in the holy wood east of Muileann chiar. Aonghas Cam, the old cutter, scores his first tally-stick through the middle and sets him cutting sticks two years before he is trusted near a beast to be counted.

events.title: Aonghas Cam's failing thread
events.body: A fever settles in the old cutter's crooked leg and will not draw out. Through that winter Rònat watches him grope after names and lines of the long teaching-thread and not always find them, and it is by that fireside, and not by any beast to be counted, that the shape of the sound-marks first comes to him.

events.title: The first name cut in strokes
events.body: Rònat cuts his own name onto a length of ash by a scheme of small strokes, one to a sound, and reads it back cold three days after. He sets the same trick to Aonghas Cam's own name and lays the stick in the old man's hand, who reads his name off it and calls it a count of sounds where he had always cut a count of fish.

events.title: The death of Aonghas Cam
events.body: The old cutter of Muileann chiar's stag school dies in his sleep, having asked that his own years be counted the old way at the last, one stroke to a year, having spent his life trusting a count over a name. Rònat cuts the tally himself.

events.title: The western teachers come east
events.body: Two teachers of the western druid school travel to the far-eastern Muileann chiar to learn Rònat's sound-marks, and stay a season under a man twenty years their junior. Among them is Sìleas nic Ruairidh, eldest of the two, who carries the scheme home and turns it over in her own mind.

events.title: The letters set against the obelisk
events.body: Rònat and two others walk five days east to the grey stone at Cnoc bheag and set the sound-marks stroke for stroke against the old marks cut there. Nothing answers: no vowel, no grouping, no order in the stone's marks matches theirs.

events.title: The first thing written of the old marks
events.body: Before the road home, Rònat cuts onto ash the finding at Cnoc bheag: that the makers of the old stone did not teach the makers of the stag's marks and are not known to them. It is the first thought, rather than a name or a count, that the new marks are made to carry.

events.title: Niall Òg at the stag's school
events.body: The ancient heir passes through the far east on foot and sits two evenings by the school's fire, telling pupils tales of the night of the handful. He asks, at the second evening's end, after the trick of marks he has heard tell of on the road.

events.title: Niall Òg reads his own name
events.body: Rònat cuts Niall Òg's name in the sound-marks and sets the stick in his hand. The old heir, who has been called by his name more times than there are fish in the western sea, reads it back within the hour and laughs until he coughs, saying he has found, at last, a name that stays after the mouth that gave it has gone home.

events.title: The chest of mismatched tallies opened
events.body: Sìleas Dhonn, new in the chair at Dùn dhearg after Dòmhnall Crùbach's death, has brought out and opened before the household the chest she has kept locked for years: her own fair copy of three seasons' Ceann mhin tallies that never matched the toll counted at the gate.

events.title: Beathan mac Dhonnchaidh's memory found wanting
events.body: The old keeper of Muileann shean recites his tally to Sìleas Dhonn from memory, the old way, name for name; she asks him plainly how she is to know it is the same tally he gave the road-guard three seasons past. He has no answer beyond his own honesty, and she sends east for a teacher of the sound-marks.

events.title: Rònat teaches Sìleas Dhonn's clerks
events.body: Rònat walks the last long road of his active years to Dùn dhearg and teaches the ruler's clerks the sound-marks over a winter, finding grown clerks trained to a column of figures quicker with the knife than any pupil he taught in the holy wood.

events.title: Ailig mac Ruairidh caught by his own gate
events.body: The keeper of Ceann mhin's toll, first summoned to render account cut in the new marks and checked against the road-guard's own cutting at his gate, is found short by a sum no honest forgetting explains. It is the first time a keeper's own tally, and not his word, answers for him before the hall.

events.title: The first whole sentence
events.body: Cutting the record of Ailig mac Ruairidh's shortfall for the hall's keeping, Rònat sets down the first whole sentence any hand has yet cut in the sound-marks: that the toll of Ceann mhin was counted short and the keeper answered for it. It stands after him in the hall, saying the same thing to every thumb that reads it.

events.title: Sìleas Dhonn dies at her ledger
events.body: Sìleas Dhonn dies in the chair at Dùn dhearg with a keeper's tally open on her knee, in her hundred and ninety-fourth year. She has asked that the chair stand its customary night and day and no longer, having had forty years at her uncle's side to learn the feel of it.

events.title: Iain Garbh's demand sent south
events.body: On his first morning in the chair Iain Garbh reads Caol leathan's thin account and sends a rider south with a plain demand in his own hand: the toll owed in full, counted before Dùn dhearg's own man at the harbour, or an answer for why it should not be paid.

events.title: The basket set on the hall floor
events.body: Iain Garbh's rider returns from Caol leathan white about the mouth, carrying a covered basket he will not open himself. Iain lifts the lid to find it packed in rows with fish-bones, picked clean, and no letter with it.

events.title: Iain Garbh calls the levy
events.body: Iain Garbh laughs once over the basket of fish-bones, then calls the road-guards from every waypoint within three days' ride and tells the lowland households their levy stands, raising his voice at no one the whole of that week.

events.title: Iain Garbh folds the Keeper's answer
events.body: Iain Garbh's messengers return from Dùn ìseal empty-handed, made to repeat Uisdean mac Ruairidh's refusal word for word. Iain folds the written answer once and puts it inside his coat, and never again sets foot on the Hall's ground.

events.title: The coughing winter at Muileann òg
events.body: The warband winters on peat smoke at the burned toll-house of Muileann òg. Men who marched south whole come home in spring with a cough some of them carry the rest of their days, so that the older road-guards are known ever after by the sound of a hard winter's night.
